source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting company losses in a financial disclosure

1. Start with the accounting records.
2.
completion:
2. Identify loss-related transactions: Review financial records such as general ledgers, journals, and trial balances to identify transactions that represent losses. This could include declines in asset values (e.g., inventory write-downs), bad debts, operational losses, or other extraordinary items.

3. Categorize the losses: Classify the losses according to your accounting policies and financial reporting standards. This may include operational losses, financial losses (e.g., interest rate swaps), impairments, and other comprehensive income (OCI) items. Be sure to distinguish between one-time and recurring losses.

4. Measure the losses: Quantify each loss. Follow accounting standards (such as GAAP or IFRS) when valuing impairments, write-downs, and other loss-related transactions. Use consistent measurement principles across all loss categories.

5. Gain approval from management: Ensure that senior management reviews and approves the documentation of losses. This review should cover the identification, classification
